document: Passport (valid for the whole planned stay) and a copy of all used pages
why_plain_english: The office checks who you are and that your passport stays valid.

document: One recent biometric passport photo (35 x 45 mm)
why_plain_english: It goes on your residence card.

document: Residence permit application form (signed)
why_plain_english: This is the actual application. We pre-fill it and you only sign.

document: Proof that you registered your Hamburg address
why_plain_english: Everyone who moves into a flat in Germany registers the address. The confirmation is usually asked for.

document: Rental contract and the landlord's move-in confirmation
why_plain_english: Shows where you live. The landlord's confirmation is also needed for the address registration.

document: Proof of health insurance
why_plain_english: Health insurance is required for everyone living in Germany.

document: Copy of the entry visa you travelled on
why_plain_english: Shows how you entered. (In this illustrative rule set, US and Japanese nationals apply after arriving, so they skip this.)

document: Certified translations of documents that are not in German or English
why_plain_english: Offices usually only read German or English. A certified translator can help.

permit_types: EU Blue Card|§18b skilled worker|ICT card
document: Signed employment contract or binding job offer
why_plain_english: Shows the job you are coming for.

document: Employer's declaration about the job (salary and hours)
why_plain_english: A standard form your employer fills in. We ask HR for it directly.

document: University degree certificate and transcript
why_plain_english: Shows your qualification.

document: Recognition or comparability statement for your degree
why_plain_english: Shows that your degree is comparable to a German one, if it isn't already listed as recognised.

document: Assignment letter from your company (role and duration of the transfer)
why_plain_english: Explains the transfer within the company. We ask HR for it directly.

document: Proof that you have worked for the company group for some time before the transfer
why_plain_english: Intra-company transfers are for people already with the company. We ask HR for it directly.

document: CV and proof of your qualification as a manager or specialist
why_plain_english: Shows you fit the role you are being sent for.

document: Marriage certificate (with apostille or legalisation if needed)
why_plain_english: Shows the family relationship.

document: Copy of your partner's residence permit or passport
why_plain_english: Shows your partner's right to live in Germany.

document: Proof that the flat is big enough for the family
why_plain_english: The office checks there is enough living space for everyone.

document: Basic German certificate (level A1)
why_plain_english: Often asked for when joining a partner. (In this illustrative rule set, some nationalities, including US and Japanese, skip it.)

document: University admission letter
why_plain_english: Shows the study place.

document: Proof of funds (for example a blocked-account confirmation)
why_plain_english: Shows you can cover living costs while studying.

document: Proof of language skills for your course (German or English)
why_plain_english: The university and the office check you can follow the course.
